celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿وَالسَّمَاءِ وَالطَّارِقِ﴾: originally, anyone who comes by night; from this are the stars, because they rise at night.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ﴾ — made you know — ﴿مَا الطَّارِقُ﴾: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of the second object of «أدرى»; and what comes after the first «ما» is its khabar. In it is a magnifying of the matter of the ṭāriq, which is explained by what follows it: it is

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿النَّجْمُ﴾, that is, the Pleiades or any star, ﴿الثَّاقِبُ﴾: the shining, because it pierces the darkness with its light. And the answer to the oath is:

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿إِنْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ لَمَا عَلَيْهَا حَافِظٌ﴾: with «ما» lightened, it is redundant (mazīda), and «إن» is lightened (mukhaffafa) from the heavy «إنّ», its noun being omitted, that is, «إنه», and the lām is the differentiating lām (fāriqa). With it doubled [لَمَّا], «إن» is negating (nāfiya) and «لمّا» means «إلا» ("except"). The guardian is from the angels; he guards its deeds, good and evil.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿فَلْيَنْظُرِ الْإِنْسَانُ﴾ with a look of reflection ﴿مِمَّ خُلِقَ﴾: from what thing. Its answer:

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿خُلِقَ مِنْ مَاءٍ دَافِقٍ﴾: possessing a gushing forth, from the man and the woman, into her womb,

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿يَخْرُجُ مِنْ بَيْنِ الصُّلْبِ﴾ of the man ﴿وَالتَّرَائِبِ﴾ of the woman, which are the bones of the chest.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ — He, Exalted is He — ﴿عَلَى رَجْعِهِ﴾ — raising man after his death — ﴿لَقَادِرٌ﴾. So when he reflects on his origin, he knows that the One able to do that is able to raise him.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿يَوْمَ تُبْلَى﴾: are tested and laid bare ﴿السَّرَائِرُ﴾: the hidden things of the hearts in beliefs and intentions.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿فَمَا لَهُ﴾ — the one who denies the Resurrection — ﴿مِنْ قُوَّةٍ﴾ by which to protect himself from the punishment ﴿وَلَا نَاصِرٍ﴾ to ward it off from him.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿وَالسَّمَاءِ ذَاتِ الرَّجْعِ﴾: the rain, because it returns time after time,

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ ذَاتِ الصَّدْعِ﴾: the splitting open for plants.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾, that is, the Qur'an, ﴿لَقَوْلٌ فَصْلٌ﴾: it separates truth from falsehood,

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾, that is, the disbelievers, ﴿يَكِيدُونَ كَيْدًا﴾: they devise plots against the Prophet ﷺ,

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿وَأَكِيدُ كَيْدًا﴾: I lead them on step by step from where they do not know.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿فَمَهِّلِ﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿الْكَافِرِينَ أَمْهِلْهُمْ﴾: a tawkīd (emphasis) made graceful by the difference in wording; that is, give them respite ﴿رُوَيْدًا﴾: a little. It is a maṣdar (verbal noun) emphasizing the meaning of the governing word (ʿāmil), the diminutive of «رود» or of «إرواد» by way of tarkhīm (truncation). Allah the Exalted seized them at Badr, and the respite was abrogated by the Verse of the Sword, that is, the command to fight and wage jihad.
